title: Mowgli
author: Rudyard Kipling
short_summary: A man-cub named Mowgli is found alone in the Indian jungle and raised by a pack of wolves. Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther become his teachers and friends, showing him the Law of the Jungle. But the tiger Shere Khan, who hates humans, wants Mowgli gone — and the boy must decide whether he truly belongs among the wolves, or with his own kind.
extended_summary:
A man-cub named Mowgli is found alone in the Indian jungle and raised by a pack of wolves. Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther become his teachers and friends, showing him the Law of the Jungle. But the tiger Shere Khan, who hates humans, wants Mowgli gone — and the boy must decide whether he truly belongs among the wolves, or with his own kind.

As Mowgli grows, he learns to speak with the animals and earns their respect through courage rather than strength. When Shere Khan finally corners him, Mowgli outwits the tiger using fire — the one thing every jungle creature fears — and proves himself a leader in his own right. Eventually, drawn by curiosity about the human village nearby, Mowgli must choose between the only family he's known and the world he was born into.

questions.prompt: Who raises Mowgli after he is found alone in the jungle?
questions.explanation: A wolf pack adopts Mowgli as one of their own cubs.

questions.prompt: Match each character to their role in Mowgli's life.

right: Teaches him the Law of the Jungle
Watches over him as a quiet guide
Wants him gone from the jungle

questions.explanation: Baloo teaches the rules, Bagheera protects quietly, Shere Khan is the threat, and Mowgli faces the central choice.

questions.prompt: Every creature in the jungle fears one thing above all: ___.
questions.explanation: Mowgli uses fire, which he calls the 'red flower,' to defeat Shere Khan.

questions.prompt: Sort each character into the right group.
questions.explanation: Baloo, Bagheera, and the wolf pack raise and protect Mowgli, while Shere Khan is his one real enemy.

questions.prompt: Do you think Mowgli belongs more with the wolves or with humans? Explain your thinking.
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — Mowgli is shaped by both worlds, and the story leaves the choice open.

questions.prompt: Mowgli earns the jungle's respect through one thing above all. What is it?

options: Being the fastest runner in the jungle

questions.explanation: Mowgli is smaller and weaker than most jungle animals — it's his courage, not his muscles, that earns their respect.

questions.prompt: Mowgli calls fire the '___ flower' — the one thing every creature in the jungle fears.
questions.explanation: It's Mowgli's own nickname for fire, and the key to how he finally outwits Shere Khan.

questions.prompt: Put Mowgli's path through the jungle in order.

items: Wolves find and raise Mowgli as one of their own cubs
Baloo and Bagheera teach him the Law of the Jungle
Mowgli outwits Shere Khan using fire
Mowgli must decide whether he belongs with the wolves or with humans

questions.explanation: Each stage builds toward the same question the story leaves open at the end: where does Mowgli really belong?

questions.prompt: Match each teacher to the lesson they give Mowgli.

right: Teaches him the Law of the Jungle directly
Protects him quietly, without needing thanks
Raises him and gives him a family
Teaches him, without meaning to, what real danger looks like

questions.explanation: Even Mowgli's enemy ends up teaching him something — just not on purpose.

questions.prompt: Sort each statement into the right group.

content.groupA: True about the Law of the Jungle, as Mowgli learns it
content.groupB: Not true about the Law of the Jungle

options.label: Courage matters more than raw strength
Every creature in the jungle fears fire
The strongest animal always makes the rules
Humans and jungle animals never have anything to learn from each other

questions.explanation: Two of these sound like they could be jungle rules but are actually the opposite of what Mowgli's story teaches.

questions.prompt: Mowgli has to choose between the jungle family that raised him and the human world he was born into. If you were Mowgli, what's one question you'd want answered before making that choice?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the story leaves Mowgli's choice open on purpose, so there's no single right question either.
